newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unilever launches French CD-Rom promotion.
newsitem.headline: Unilever launches French CD-Rom promotion.

text.p: Unilever AS/Plc UNVR.L on Thursday brought a CD-Rom promoting detergents to France, where households with multimedia equipment are scarce.

The CD-Rom, already launched in Britain, Norway, Sweden and Denmark, costs the company much less than conventional advertising, Loic Tardy, head of Unilever's French unit, Lever France, told a news conference.

Tardy expects the CD-Rom, which includes advice on removing stains and a computer game for children, to interest multimedia enthusiasts rather than existing customers for the company's French detergent Skip.
"The CD-Rom will not so much interest Skip users but people equipped for multimedia. We hope they will stay with Skip," he said.
In France 15 percent of households have a home computer, and a third of those are equipped to use multimedia products, he said.
Skip has 11 percent of the six-billion-franc French detergent market and will shortly run a television campaign promoting its liquid detergent.
It shares the market with all the multinational players, each seeking to grab share on grounds of colour-fastness, toughness on stains or kindness to babies' skin.
Skip claims to be the first detergent brand in France to use a CD-Rom as a promotion tool.
Lever France has made 10,000 CD-Roms, which will be distributed by post and by IBM France with its Aptiva multimedia home computer, Tardy said.
